title: v0 Design Systems 2.0: Design System as a Skill, v0.json Configuration
content:
# v0 Design Systems 2.0

"Design Systems 2.0 lets you teach v0 your design system once, so chats can build with your real components, tokens, and conventions."

The abstraction change from v0's legacy registry approach: a design system is saved as a **skill** in your current scope (team or personal workspace). Skills are focused instruction sets v0 keeps with your work and applies when relevant.

## Required sources

- Installable npm package, .tgz/.tar archive, or source directory
- Design system repository or package containing components and tokens
- **A real app consuming the system** (shows providers, styles, fonts, setup)
- Storybook, docs, or design guidelines
- Figma frames or nodes for visual reference
- Private package credentials (as Development shared environment variables)
- Installation instructions and usage examples

## Import process

1. Add sources on the Design Systems page: GitHub repos, Figma frames/nodes, links, attachments
2. Add environment variables for private packages (requires Developer role on Vercel minimum)
3. Add notes about global styles, providers, fonts, deprecated components, conventions
4. Review the starter app v0 builds before saving
5. Approve and save the skill

## v0.json

    {
      "version": 1,
      "referenceWorkspace": {
        "sources": [
          {
            "id": "github-repo:owner/repo:main",
            "type": "github-repo",
            "repo": { "org": "owner", "name": "repo" },
            "ref": "main",
            "mountPath": "/vercel/share/v0-reference-workspace-sources/owner/repo/main"
          }
        ]
      },
      "environment": {
        "providers": [
          { "type": "shared-env-vars", "ids": ["env_var_id"] }
        ]
      },
      "starter": {
        "source": "skill-directory",
        "path": "assets/starter"
      }
    }

- version — schema version (use 1)
- referenceWorkspace.sources — **up to three** read-only GitHub sources, each with repo, ref, id, mount path. The three-source cap is a real constraint for multi-repo design systems.
- environment.providers — env var linking, typically shared-env-vars with Development IDs, or vercel-project with a projectId
- starter — application template: skill-directory, v0-default, or empty

## Using and updating

Saved skills appear on the Design Systems page. Attach from the prompt toolbar or reference in prompts. "Team owners on paid plans can choose a default design system for the team"; manual selections override the default.

Update by asking v0 in any chat to apply changes; v0 re-validates the starter app. Critically: "existing projects retain their original code; only new chats pick up the updated version." v0 does not retroactively migrate generated work.

## Access control

On paid team plans, owners can restrict skill creation/editing to "Owners and selected members." All members can still view and use skills. Only team owners set defaults.

## Best practices

- Include both the source and at least one real consumer app
- Prefer current docs and working examples over stale references
- Document global setup: "providers, theme wrappers, fonts, CSS imports, Tailwind config, and required environment variables"
- Keep sources focused on one design system and framework stack
- Pin GitHub sources to branches/refs and package versions in package.json

The "include a real consumer app" guidance is the practically important one: v0 is stating that a component package alone does not convey providers, theme wrappers, and global CSS setup — the agent learns those from an example app, not from the library.
